mythologySignificance:
Kashi (Varanasi) is praised across Puranas as the city of light where Shiva as Vishwanath is the eternal lord. The Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga stands at the spiritual centre of this sacred geography. Texts such as the Kashi Khanda (Skanda Purana tradition) describe liberation (moksha) associated with dying in Kashi under Shiva’s grace.

Pilgrimage literature treats Kashi Vishwanath Temple as a tirtha — a crossing where devotion to Lord Shiva (Vishwanath) is believed to bear fruit more readily than in ordinary space. Accounts summarised here follow widely cited epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya traditions; temple priests remain the guides for ritual detail.
localBeliefs:
Banaras belief treats the Ganga aarti, the lanes to Vishwanath, and the cremation ghats as a continuous sacred theatre — life, death, and liberation in one city. Local devotion holds that Vishwanath’s glance frees the soul.

The expanded temple corridor has become part of contemporary pilgrimage memory, while older neighbourhood shrines and Annapurna traditions remain woven into everyday Banarsi faith.
